title: Removing six SST input step shapes retains 14% of linear trend information in 1982-2022 under equal independent errors
abstract: We tested SST feedback estimates without choosing input-step amplitudes. A common trend estimator removes six known step shapes and their transition months. Under equal independent errors, it retains 13.63% of linear trend information in 1982-2022 and 14.44% in 2001-2022. We prove the minimum variance bound for unbiased linear estimators with these constraints. The standard error cost is 2.71-fold and 2.63-fold. In published series from five model Green functions, raw and corrected SST versions then agree to numerical precision. This is a design property, not correction validation. The ordinary 1982-2022 DOISST pattern-radiation trend has negative conditional block intervals in all five models. After the six-date constraint, one model excludes zero with 36-month blocks and none does with 24- or 60-month blocks. The 1985-2004 interval holds 84% of squared estimator weights. These results show the information cost of an amplitude-free test. The method changes temporal emphasis and removes real climate changes with step-like shapes. It is not a corrected historical trajectory. Fixed linear Green functions, shared observations and conditional residual uncertainty limit inference. Code, weights, aggregate results, bootstrap draws, source hashes and verified retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Known-date step immunity removes 86% of independent-error trend information. Product gaps can remain, and the negative pattern-radiation trend becomes uncertain in most models.

citations.reason: Verified monthly SST and radiation-response series and uniform response constants. Tests the evidence without step amplitudes.
Known DOISST dates read from verified box_steps.npz.
